about: The cases the answer ceiling is held to, which its TypeScript twin answers alike. A piece of text is a string, or a text and how many times it repeats; a case's items are its pieces taken `copies` times over. Every letter outside ASCII counts as one character, whatever its bytes.

items.name: a list that fits comes back whole
a list over the ceiling is cut to whole items
items.note: -- cut at the 100-character ceiling: 10 of 40 nodes. For the other 30: ask with narrower words.

items.name: counts of a thousand and over are grouped
items.note: -- cut at the 100-character ceiling: 10 of 4,000 nodes. For the other 3,990: ask with narrower words.

items.name: one item alone over the ceiling leaves nothing
items.note: -- one of the nodes alone is over the 100-character ceiling, so nothing was given. ask with narrower words.

items.name: characters are code points
items.note: -- cut at the 10-character ceiling: 1 of 2 lines. For the other 1: ask over a narrower range.

items.name: the standing ceiling, grouped
items.note: -- cut at the 30,000-character ceiling: 300 of 400 rows. For the other 100: give a LIMIT.

items.name: the ceiling holds what would be printed, separators and all
items.note: -- cut at the 20-character ceiling: 2 of 3 nodes. For the other 1: ask with narrower words.

values.name: a value that fits stands as it is
a long value is cut where it stands
what was cut is counted in code points
